purpose: Teach: 戦隊/唐辛子/車いす/垣根/熱海/ウェディング/アロハ/ミント

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが戦隊ものをお孫様と観てらしたぞ
lines.en: You know, when I was young, your father used to watch those hero shows with the grandkids.
lines.style: Soft, reaching back into memory. Gentle pause before 'when I was young' — nostalgia settling in. Quiet certainty. Not mournful, but tender with distance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、唐辛子のお料理がお好きでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your grandfather — he loved spicy food, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, gently correcting the thread. A small smile underneath. Speaking to him as if he's right there listening. The affectionate patience of long marriage.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お母様が車いすで生活されたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your mother lived her life in a wheelchair.
lines.style: Lower, more weighted. The memory carries something sobering. Spoken with respect, not pity. A pause to let it settle — her strength, not her limitation.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お庭の垣根を刈り込まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather trimmed the garden hedge with such care, remember, dear?
lines.style: Gentle redirect, almost protective. She's meeting him where memory touches — the quiet actions that showed love. Soft, recognizing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと熱海に旅行したぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your father and I took a trip to Atami together.
lines.style: Clearer now, more present. The warmth of a shared memory — two of them, not a memory *of* someone. Lighter breath. Still reflective but less distant.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様のウェディングを楽しみにしてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather was so looking forward to your grandchild's wedding, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: A shift toward joy — looking forward, not backward. Still tender, but there's brightness here. Acknowledging what he cared about, what mattered to him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがアロハシャツでハワイに行かれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your father went to Hawaii in an aloha shirt.
lines.style: A small lightness enters — the image of him, vivid and particular. Not sad, but rich with detail. A smile in the voice, almost affectionate amusement at the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、夏はミントティーを召し上がってらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather always had mint tea in the summer, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Closing gently. The smallest things remembered — taste, season, habit. Voice softens further, almost a whisper. The intimacy of knowing what he loved, still holding it close.
